title: Point blowups resolve rational Gorenstein surface singularities
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative normal Nagata local domain of dimension $2$ defining a rational singularity [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-per-rational-surface-singularity]. Assume its maximal-ideal-adic completion is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Assume $R$ is Gorenstein, meaning it has finite injective dimension as a module over itself. Then there is a finite sequence $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of ordinary blowups at singular closed points above the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Every intervening scheme is integral and normal and has only finitely many singular points; the local rings at those points are again rational, Gorenstein, normal local domains of dimension $2$ with normal completion. The endpoint $X_n$ is regular, and the composite is proper and induces an isomorphism of function fields [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sc-function-field]. Length zero is allowed.
